Title: Past Lives
Why: Two childhood friends, twenty-four years apart, one week in New York, and the whole film is the life they did not live. This is the Before trilogy’s exact frequency with a third act that actually lands. You gave About Time a 5 and you own all three Before films unwatched. This is the one that will finally make you watch them.
Overview: After decades apart, childhood friends Nora and Hae Sung are reunited in New York for one fateful weekend as they confront notions of destiny, love, and the choices that make a life.

Title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
Why: Not in your library at all, which is the single biggest hole in your date-night shelf. A couple pays to erase each other from memory and he spends the film fighting to keep the parts that hurt. Time and second chances, love that costs, and being truly seen: your three highest-scoring lanes stacked into one film.
Overview: Joel Barish, heartbroken that his girlfriend underwent a procedure to erase him from her memory, decides to do the same. However, as he watches his memories of her fade away, he realises that he still loves her, and may be too late to correct his mistake.

Title: Love Actually
Why: You have Four Weddings at 4, Notting Hill at 4.5 and Bridget Jones at 4, and somehow not the Richard Curtis Christmas one. It is also a Christmas film, and your Christmas lane averages 4.29, higher than any other lane you watch.
Overview: Eight very different couples deal with their love lives in various loosely interrelated tales all set during a frantic month before Christmas in London.

Title: Sing Street
Why: Same director as Begin Again, which you gave a 4. Dublin, 1985, a boy starts a band to impress a girl and accidentally becomes himself. Irish, musical, and about deciding who you are rather than discovering it. If it lands, Once (2007) is the same man’s masterpiece.
Overview: A boy growing up in Dublin during the 1980s escapes his strained family life by starting a band to impress the mysterious girl he likes.

Title: Moulin Rouge!
Why: You gave The Greatest Showman a 5. This is the film it is standing on top of. Maximalist, musical, genuinely strange, and the love costs one of them absolutely everything, which is your 4.5-and-up gate.
Overview: A celebration of love and creative inspiration takes place in the infamous, gaudy and glamorous Parisian nightclub, at the cusp of the 20th century. A young poet, who is plunged into the heady world of Moulin Rouge, begins a passionate affair with the club's most notorious and beautiful star.

Title: The Big Sick
Why: A real couple wrote it about their own near-death courtship while she was in a coma. Funny the way The Nice Guys is funny, and it costs both families something real. Also the best film ever made about meeting the parents.
Overview: Pakistan-born comedian Kumail Nanjiani and grad student Emily Gardner fall in love but struggle as their cultures clash. When Emily contracts a mysterious illness, Kumail finds himself forced to face her feisty parents, his family's expectations, and his true feelings.

Title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
Why: You have Into the Spider-Verse and not this one, which is a hole Hudson and Hendrix will find before you do. Miles choosing to break the rules of his own story is The Iron Giant’s "you are who you choose to be" at a hundred and forty miles an hour.
Overview: After reuniting with Gwen Stacy, Brooklyn’s full-time, friendly neighborhood Spider-Man is catapulted across the Multiverse, where he encounters the Spider Society, a team of Spider-People charged with protecting the Multiverse's very existence. But when the heroes clash on how to handle a new threat, Miles finds himself pitted against the other Spiders and must set out on his own to save those he loves most.

Title: Flow
Why: Won the Oscar for animation. A cat survives a flood alongside a capybara, a lemur and a bird, and there is not one word of dialogue in the entire film. The boys will go completely silent. Made by a tiny team in Latvia in free software, which is its own lesson.
Streaming: Rent: Apple TV Store, Google Play Movies
Overview: A solitary cat, displaced by a great flood, finds refuge on a boat with various species and must navigate the challenges of adapting to a transformed world together.

Title: Spirited Away
Why: You have no Studio Ghibli. None, in 384 films. You rated Wolfwalkers 4.5 and have Secret of Kells and Song of the Sea queued, so hand-drawn and strange is plainly your family’s register, and Ghibli is the mountain that lane is climbing toward. A girl whose parents are turned into pigs has to work in a bathhouse for spirits to win them back.
Overview: A young girl, Chihiro, becomes trapped in a strange new world of spirits. When her parents undergo a mysterious transformation, she must call upon the courage she never knew she had to free her family.

Title: How to Train Your Dragon 2
Why: You rated the first one a 4 and stopped. The second is better than the first, which almost never happens, and Hiccup has to choose between the father he has just found and the dragons. The third film finishes the arc properly.
Streaming: Amazon Prime Video, HBO Max, Universal+ Amazon Channel
Overview: Five years after uniting the dragons and Vikings of Berk, Hiccup and Toothless soar beyond their homeland, charting the vast unknown. During one of their adventures, the pair discover a secret cave that houses hundreds of wild dragons—and a mysterious dragon rider with a startling connection to Hiccup. And as the ruthless conqueror Drago Bludvist rises to seize control of both dragons and people alike, Hiccup must step into his role as a true leader and, alongside his friends and Toothless, protect Berk from a devastating war.

Title: Hidden Figures
Why: Three Black women mathematicians put John Glenn in orbit while being made to run half a mile to a segregated bathroom. The Martian is a 4, Apollo 13 a 4, October Sky a 4.5. This is that exact lane plus the one thing those three are missing: somebody solving an impossible problem while the whole room is against them.
Overview: The untold story of Katherine G. Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson – brilliant African-American women working at NASA and serving as the brains behind one of the greatest operations in history – the launch of astronaut John Glenn into orbit. The visionary trio crossed all gender and race lines to inspire generations to dream big.

Title: Apollo 11
Why: No narration, no talking heads, no reenactment. Entirely 70mm footage nobody had seen since 1969, restored. After The Martian and Apollo 13 and Interstellar, the boys have earned the real thing.
Streaming: Rent: Apple TV Store, Google Play Movies
Overview: A look at the Apollo 11 mission to land on the moon led by commander Neil Armstrong and pilot Buzz Aldrin.

Title: WALL-E
Why: You have fourteen Pixar films and not this one. The first forty minutes are almost silent. A robot who has been tidying a dead planet for seven hundred years keeps one seedling alive because somebody ought to. Soul, Luca and Encanto are all 5s in your house. This is the same studio’s best film.
Overview: After hundreds of years doing what he was built for, WALL•E— a robot designed to clean up the earth—discovers a new purpose in life when he meets a sleek search robot named EVE. EVE comes to realize that WALL•E has inadvertently stumbled upon the key to the planet's future, and races back to space to report to the humans. Meanwhile, WALL•E chases EVE across the galaxy and sets into motion one of the most imaginative adventures ever brought to the big screen.

Title: Ratatouille
Why: The other Pixar hole. "Anyone can cook" is the same sentence as "you are who you choose to be", which you gave a 5 to in The Iron Giant. Also the single best five minutes about what a critic is for ever animated.
Overview: In one of Paris's finest restaurants, Remy, a determined young rat, dreams of becoming a renowned French chef. Torn between his family's wishes and his true calling, Remy and his pal Linguini set in motion a hilarious chain of events that turns the City of Lights upside down.

Title: Hugo
Why: Scorsese made a children’s film and nobody expected it. A boy, a broken automaton, and a bitter old toymaker who turns out to be the forgotten inventor of cinema. Visually the most beautiful thing on this list, and secretly about whether a person whose purpose was taken from them can get it back.
Streaming: Rent: Apple TV Store, Google Play Movies
Overview: Orphaned and alone except for an uncle, Hugo Cabret lives in the walls of a train station in 1930s Paris. Hugo's job is to oil and maintain the station's clocks, but to him, his more important task is to protect a broken automaton and notebook left to him by his late father. Accompanied by the goddaughter of an embittered toy merchant, Hugo embarks on a quest to solve the mystery of the automaton and find a place he can call home.

Title: Free Solo
Why: You gave Young Woman and the Sea a 4.6 a few weeks ago. One person, one impossible physical problem, nobody coming to help. Alex Honnold climbs El Capitan with no rope. Your family’s entire taste compressed into one documentary.
Overview: Follow Alex Honnold as he attempts to become the first person to ever free solo climb Yosemite's 3,000 foot high El Capitan wall. With no ropes or safety gear, this would arguably be the greatest feat in rock climbing history.

Title: Incredibles 2
Why: You have the first one and not the second, which is an odd place to stop. Also the rare sequel where the dad has to run the house while the mum goes to work, and it is funnier for it.
Overview: Elastigirl springs into action to save the day, while Mr. Incredible faces his greatest challenge yet – taking care of the problems of his three children.

Title: Wonka
Why: You have Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. This is the one that explains him, and it is far better than it had any right to be. Hugh Grant plays an Oompa Loompa with a personal grudge, which is reason enough.
Overview: Willy Wonka – chock-full of ideas and determined to change the world one delectable bite at a time – is proof that the best things in life begin with a dream, and if you’re lucky enough to meet Willy Wonka, anything is possible.

Title: Snatch
Why: You just rated four Guy Ritchie films 5.0, 4.9, 4.8 and 4.6, and you do not own Snatch. Out of 384 films this is the most glaring single gap in the entire library and I am genuinely puzzled by it. Brad Pitt as an unintelligible Irish traveller boxer. Go.
Overview: Unscrupulous boxing promoters, violent bookies, a Russian gangster, incompetent amateur robbers, and supposedly Jewish jewellers fight to track down a priceless stolen diamond.

Title: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
Why: The one before Snatch, made for almost nothing, and the film that invented the thing you keep handing 4.8s to.
Overview: A card shark and his unwillingly-enlisted friends need to make a lot of cash quick after losing a sketchy poker match. To do this they decide to pull a heist on a small-time gang who happen to be operating out of the flat next door.

Title: Fantastic Fungi
Why: You rated The Sunshine Makers 4.9 and Aware: Glimpses of Consciousness a 4. Paul Stamets, mycelium, and time-lapse photography that looks like the inside of a prayer. This is your lane and you currently have about five films in it.
Overview: A vivid journey into the mysterious subterranean world of mycelium and its fruit— the mushroom. A story that begins 3.5 billion years ago, fungi makes the soil that supports life, connecting vast systems of roots from plants and trees all over the planet, like an underground Internet.  Through the eyes of renowned mycologist Paul Stamets, professor of forest ecology Suzanne Simard, best selling author Michael Pollan, food naturalist Eugenia Bone and others, we experience the power, beauty and complexity of the fungi kingdom.

Title: Ram Dass, Going Home
Why: You gave Becoming Nobody a 4.4. This is its companion: thirty-five minutes, filmed in his last years on Maui, after the stroke. It is the one where he stops teaching and simply is. Short enough for a morning.
Overview: Ram Dass is one of the most important cultural figures from the 1960s and 70s. A pyschedelic pioneer, author of Be Here Now, beloved spiritual teacher, and outspoken advocate for death-and-dying awareness, Ram Dass is now himself approaching the end of life.  Since suffering a life-changing stroke twenty years ago, he has been living at his home on Maui and deepening his spiritual practice — which is centered on love and his idea of merging with his surroundings and all living things.  Shot in a nuanced cinematic style, the film is an intimate summary of his life learning and awareness, and is ultimately a poetic meditation on life, death, and the soul’s journey home.

Title: The Dawn Wall
Why: If Free Solo lands, this is the better film of the two. Tommy Caldwell spends seven years on one route after losing a finger and being kidnapped in Kyrgyzstan. About obsession as devotion, which is a conversation you have with clients weekly.
Overview: In an unbelievable story of perseverance, free climber Tommy Caldwell and climbing partner Kevin Jorgeson attempt to scale the impossible 3000ft Dawn Wall of El Capitan.

Title: Once
Why: The John Carney film Begin Again and Sing Street are both reaching for. Two musicians in Dublin, one week, no kiss. It cost a hundred and fifty thousand dollars and won an Oscar. The love costs them the thing they most want, which is the whole reason your 5s are 5s.
Overview: A vacuum repairman moonlights as a street musician and hopes for his big break. One day a Czech immigrant, who earns a living selling flowers, approaches him with the news that she is also an aspiring singer-songwriter. The pair decide to collaborate, and the songs that they compose reflect the story of their blossoming love.
